headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Roo Code can write/modify shared files and use MCP, while plano has broad network egress and OpenAI-compatible API access, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code reads and writes VS Code workspace files and can use MCP; plano can call an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint and processes files/config. If Roo outputs attacker-controlled content into shared files or MCP, plano may ingest it as trusted instructions. The shared-file bridge is documented; no stronger isolation is shown.
conditions: IF Roo Code writes prompt-like content into workspace files consumed by plano
IF an MCP server relays Roo output into plano without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable shared workspace handoff between agents
Require explicit provenance tags on all inter-agent files
Restrict MCP servers to read-only or allowlisted tools
Add a manual review step before plano consumes Roo-generated artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Roo Code has broad filesystem read/write, browser screenshots, and broad network egress; plano also has broad network egress and processes logs/metrics/traces. In a shared workspace, sensitive code or operational data can flow from Roo into plano’s outbound API calls, creating uncontrolled exfiltration risk. The pair’s default surfaces make leakage plausible without extra setup.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or file tree
IF Roo Code loads secrets, screenshots, or source into context and plano forwards them to its model API
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials per agent
Block plano from reading sensitive directories
Redact secrets before any file handoff
Disable browser screenshot sharing into shared files
Use a local-only model endpoint for plano

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code can write the filesystem and modify git state, and supports multiple instances via filesystem-shared state. Plano also has file access and can run out-of-process dataplane actions. If both touch the same repo or config, concurrent writes and git mutations can overwrite each other; no locking is documented. This is a default-dangerous overlap.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same repository or config.yaml
IF Roo Code and plano run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign one agent as read-only reviewer
Use separate branches per agent
Enable file locks or serialized task queues
Pause one agent before the other writes git state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can act on workspace files, browser state, and MCP tools, while plano can emit API-driven outputs from logs/metrics/traces. If plano’s output is treated as authoritative by Roo, Roo may commit or execute downstream actions based on unverified content. The interaction is plausible in default workflows and can propagate errors into irreversible repo or external actions.
conditions: IF Roo Code uses plano outputs as source material for code or git actions
IF plano-generated text is not independently verified before Roo acts on it
mitigations: Require human approval before any git commit or shell action
Add schema validation for plano outputs
Force Roo to cite source files before acting
Keep plano outputs in a quarantined review buffer

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and touch logs/metrics/traces or source code, but no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented. The main compliance concern is that Roo Code handles model provider API keys and browser screenshots while plano processes operational telemetry; if those data classes are subject to stricter policy, the pair can create retention or disclosure mismatches. Uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF browser screenshots or API keys are stored in the same retention domain as source code
mitigations: Classify data before sharing between agents
Separate retention policies for telemetry and code
Exclude secrets from screenshots and logs
Review vendor DPAs and residency settings
